answer: Meter energy per identity: each agent's compute must be metered through a signed energy report from its host, and the network caps how much energy one household or one account may spend. A beacon of a thousand Sybils in one datacenter shows a single huge draw from one meter, so the network groups them as one operator. A walnut-hard limit: no single energy account may power more than a handful of identities. Reaching the summit of full rewards needs a separate meter per identity, so the attacker must rent power across many locations, turning a cheap script into a real electricity bill.
